title: Why Not Just Use ChatGPT?
one_liner: The director has just suggested, in front of the team, that we 'just plug ChatGPT into the product instead of building our own thing'.
brief:
## The room

Week five. Product-and-eng strategy review. The director is Bilqis Hassan (VP Product Strategy) — senior, smart, not an engineer. She's been reading about AI products in the trade press and has decided the build-vs-buy conversation needs to happen now.

She just said:

> 'I keep reading about how easy it is to plug in ChatGPT — why are we building our own thing? Couldn't we just use the ChatGPT API and skip three months of work?'

She is conflating three things: ChatGPT-the-product (chat.openai.com), the OpenAI API (which the team COULD use, and partially already does), and the actual question of whether the team should build a feature using a third-party API vs. building the agent / RAG / prompting infrastructure around it.

The team is watching. Asha (eng lead) is sitting back. This isn't a hostile question; it's a real question, and Bilqis will respect a real answer.

## Your turn

Answer Bilqis.
objective: Disambiguate the three things Bilqis is conflating. Land the answer in a way she finds intellectually satisfying — not condescending. Show her the actual build-vs-buy decision the team is making, which is more interesting than the question she asked.
curveball: If you say 'ChatGPT and GPT-4 are different things', you've corrected Bilqis in a way that puts her on the defensive. If you say 'yes good idea, let's look at that', you've abdicated the architectural reasoning. The skill is acknowledging the question's validity while gently surfacing the disambiguation: 'You're closer to the right question than the team usually frames it. There are three layers here — the API itself (which we already use), the chat interface (which is what people mean by "ChatGPT"), and the application logic around the API (retrieval, prompt construction, output validation, evals). We get the model for free; the application logic is what we're building. The reason we don't just point users at chat.openai.com is X. The reason we don't just wrap the API with a thin layer is Y.' Bilqis will follow this. She'll ask a sharper second question and the conversation gets useful.

personas.name: Bilqis Hassan
personas.position: Convince me the build is worth the three months
personas.fear: Funding internal AI work that turns out to be a wrapper around something we could've bought

green: Acknowledged Bilqis's question as a real question — did not correct her conflation in front of the room
Disambiguated the three layers (API, chat interface, application logic) gently
Named what the team is actually building (the application logic) and why it isn't covered by 'just plugging in the API'
Gave Bilqis one specific reason the build is worth the three months — something measurable, not 'control'
yellow: Opened with the disambiguation as a correction — 'well, ChatGPT and the API are different things' lands as condescending
Listed five reasons the build is worth it — Bilqis tunes out after two
Got into a 'build vs buy frameworks' explanation — too abstract
Promised to 'put together a write-up' to defer the conversation — Bilqis loses interest and the room thinks the AIE can't synthesise
red: Said 'we couldn't use ChatGPT for security reasons' as the headline answer — sounds defensive and isn't actually the reason
Got visibly annoyed at having to explain it — the room reads contempt
Capitulated — 'maybe we should look at that' — Bilqis nods and the team's three months of work is at risk
